spots.name: Palace of Peace and Reconciliation
spots.summary: The Palace of Peace and Reconciliation, also translated as the Pyramid of Peace and Accord, is a 62-metre-high (203 ft) pyramid in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan, that serves as a non-denominational national spiritual centre and event venue.

spots.name: Baiterek
spots.summary: Baiterek is a monument and observation tower in Astana, the capital city of Kazakhstan. A tourist attraction popular with foreign visitors and Kazakhs, it is emblematic of the city, which became capital of the country in 1997.

spots.name: Nursultan Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Nursultan Mosque is a mosque in Astana, Kazakhstan. It is the largest mosque in Central Asia, the second largest mosque outside the Middle East, and one of the largest in the world.

spots.name: National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan
spots.summary: The National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan (Kazakh: Қазақстан Республикасының Ұлттық музейі, romanized: Qazaqstan Respublikasynyñ Ūlttyq muzeiı), is located in Astana. When it was built in 2014, it was the largest museum in Central Asia.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan

spots.name: Abu Dhabi Plaza
spots.summary: Abu Dhabi Plaza is a mixed-use development complex in the very center of Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan. As of 2022, the tallest tower of Abu Dhabi Plaza at 310.8 metres (1,020 ft) is the tallest building in Kazakhstan and Central Asia.

spots.name: Nurjol Boulevard
spots.summary: The Nurjol Boulevard, formerly known as Green Water Boulevard is a pedestrian zone in the business and administrative center on the left bank of Ishim river in Astana. The Boulevard is one of the main attractions of the city and country.

spots.name: Hazrat Sultan Mosque
spots.summary: The Hazrat Sultan Mosque is a Friday mosque in Astana, Kazakhstan.

spots.name: Nur-Astana Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Nur-Astana Mosque, is a mosque in Astana, Kazakhstan. It is third largest mosque in Central Asia. The 40-meter (131-foot) height symbolizes the age of the Islamic prophet Muhammad when he received the revelations, and the height of the minarets are 63 meters, the age Muhammad was when he died.

spots.name: Our Mother of Perpetual Help Cathedral, Astana

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Our Mother of Perpetual Help Cathedral is the Catholic Cathedral of Astana, Kazakhstan, and the headquarters of the Archdiocese of Mary Most Holy in Astana.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Our Mother of Perpetual Help Cathedral, Astana

spots.name: Astana Opera
spots.summary: Astana Opera is an opera house in Astana, Kazakhstan, on the basis of an executive order of Nursultan Nazarbayev.

spots.name: Astana Arena
spots.summary: The Astana Arena is a football stadium in Astana, Kazakhstan. The stadium holds 30,000 and has a retractable roof. It serves as the national stadium for the Kazakhstan national football team.

spots.name: Independence Square, Astana
spots.summary: Independence Square also referred to as Kazakh Eli Square, is the main square in Astana, Kazakhstan.

spots.name: Qaraötkel Bridge
spots.summary: The Qaraötkel Bridge, also known as Ramstor Bridge is an arch bridge spanning the Ishim River in Astana, Kazakhstan. It was built between 2007 and 2008 as a road bridge crossing the Ishim River.

photo.author: Peretz Partensky from San Francisco, USA

spots.name: Kazakhstan Central Concert Hall
spots.summary: The Central Concert Hall is a center for performing arts in Astana, the capital city of Kazakhstan. It was designed by Italian architect Manfredi Nicoletti and inaugurated by the President of Kazakhstan, Nursultan Nazarbayev, on the nation's Independence Day, 15 December, in 2009.

spots.name: Grand Alatau
spots.summary: Grand Alatau is a residential building complex situated in Astana, Kazakhstan. The development consists of four high-rise buildings, the tallest of which reaches a height of 153 m (502 ft) and contains 43 floors. As of 2026, the 43-story tower currently stands as the tallest residential building in Kazakhstan.

spots.name: Mäñgılık El Triumphal Arch
spots.summary: Mäñgılık El is a 20-meter-tall triumphal arch located in Astana, Kazakhstan. The monument was inaugurated on 16 December 2011, marking the 20th anniversary of Kazakhstan’s independence. It was initiated by the country’s first president, Nursultan Nazarbayev.

spots.name: Lovers' Park
spots.summary: Lovers' Park, also known as Youth Park is an urban park in Astana, Kazakhstan. It was opened on 6 July 2005 on the Capital City Day celebration. The park is located right behind the KazMunayGas headquarters and is situated right between Döñgelek Square and in the front of Khan Shatyr.

spots.name: Botanical Garden
spots.summary: The Astana Botanical Garden is the largest botanical garden in the city of Astana, Kazakhstan, which features a pond with fountains and three bridges. About 9,000 trees and shrubs from Europe, Asia and North America have been planted, with bicycle and jogging paths laid among the green areas.

spots.name: Otan Qorgaushylar Monument
spots.summary: Otan Korgaushilar Monument is a city memorial in Astana, the capital of Kazakhstan. It is in Defenders of the Fatherland Square near Tauelsizdik Avenue. It primarily commemorates the Kazakhs who were sent to serve in the Soviet Army during the Great Patriotic War as well as veterans of the Kazakh Armed Forces.

spots.name: The Museum of the First President of the Republic of Kazakhstan
spots.summary: The Museum of the First President of the Republic of Kazakhstan is a museum situated in Astana. It was established by Decree of the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan on August 28, 2004. It is located on 11 Beibitshilik Street, in Astana.
spots.wikipediaTitle: The Museum of the First President of the Republic of Kazakhstan

spots.name: Barys Arena
spots.summary: Barys Arena is a multi-purpose indoor arena located in Astana, Kazakhstan. It serves as a home arena for Barys Astana in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL). The arena seats 11,578 spectators for ice hockey.

spots.name: Döñgelek Square
spots.summary: Döñgelek Square is a city square in Astana, Kazakhstan. It was created in 2003. The square is located in front of KazMunayGas headquarters and features many shops and restaurants. The square is built in two tiers. The lower one is designed for pedestrians, and the upper one is intended for vehicles.

spots.name: Kazhymukan Munaitpasov Stadium
spots.summary: Kajymukan Munaitpasov Stadium is a multi-purpose stadium in Astana, Kazakhstan. It is named after the Kazakh wrestler Kazhymukan Munaitpasov. He was the first Kazakh who became a world champion. The stadium is currently used mostly for association football matches and is the home stadium of FC Zhenis.

spots.name: National Academic Library of the Republic of Kazakhstan

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The National Academic Library of Kazakhstan is a national library specializing in academic publications. Built during the presidency of National Library of Kazakhstan, the structure resembles a Möbius strip.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Academic Library of the Republic of Kazakhstan

spots.name: Atameken miniature park

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An outdoor museum giving you an overview of the entire country in a miniature version. This 1.7-hectare exhibit features more than 200 mock-up pieces, creating Kazakh cities and historical memorials. During the summer months at least, there are normally English speaking guides available (optional obviously), should you wish to learn a little about the models, and there is a covered section which f

spots.name: Harat's Irish Pub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Astana's Irish-style pub. Quite popular among expats, although the crowd still overwhelmingly skews local as there are not that many expats in Astana. Not the cheapest place in the city, but has live music a lot of nights and usually has a good crowd later in the evening. The block near Harat's has a lot of bars close to the river and is generally a good place to find yourself in the summer when y

spots.name: Ali Babas
spots.summary: Popular summer restaurant. The waitresses and waiters dress in traditional dress and the menu offers a selection of central Asian cuisine. Prices are in line with Europe or America but the food is good. Fake bird cages hang from the roof which tweet electronically. Camel and horse milk are on offer alongside Leffe beer.

spots.name: Line Brew

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Line Brew is a relatively well-known beer brand across the city. Primarily a restaurant during the day, though as the evening turns to night it becomes more bar than steak house. Quite expensive and a reservation is recommended on Friday/Saturday nights.

spots.name: Dark Side

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An upscale cocktail bar, very popular among young people in Astana. Gets very busy on Fridays, Saturdays, and on Wednesdays when they run "2 for 1" on cocktails. May struggle to get a table on these nights without a reservation.

spots.name: Nirvana

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cheap and cheerful nightclub. Very basic compared to some of the preferred, more upscale establishments in the city, but close to a lot of bars and usually gets quite busy every day of the week; more so around 1 AM.

spots.name: Melnitsa
spots.summary: Ukrainian restaurant with large dining areas. Lots of traditional dishes like potato pancakes and of course Chicken Kyiv. Live music in the evenings. Fresh bread oven. Great décor, like a farmer's hut.

spots.name: Winners Pub

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hidden gem" of a bar within spitting distance of Baiterek Tower. Very reasonably priced considering its prime location. Also offers Shisha and Karaoke.

spots.name: Turfan
spots.summary: Popular cafe with Turkish and other Central Asian food. Limited English, just point to the menu pictures. Alcohol served except in Ramadan.

spots.name: Saksaul

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Restaurant with Kazakh cuisine and menu also in English. Good choice, although the staff doesn't seem professional all the time.

spots.name: Rafe
spots.summary: A modern coffee bar offering Italian food with a twist. Be sure to check out the horse pizza. A few other cafés around town.

spots.name: Sattj
spots.summary: Serves mainly Kazakh food, with some European.

spots.name: Cafe Shymkent
spots.summary: Cheap and cheerful place.

spots.name: Sunduk

hours.note: Closed Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Central Asian cuisine.
